decisions.what: PostgreSQL runs as a compose service with a named volume and healthcheck; DATABASE_URL alone switches to a managed host later.
decisions.why: Cheapest for a first VPS deploy. Keeps the ticket's requirement that the database host can change.

decisions.what: A one-shot migrate service runs goose over the four dirs, then exits. web and poller wait on service_completed_successfully.
decisions.why: Gives the ticket's wait-for-Postgres ordering. One command deploys. No half-migrated database.

decisions.what: Caddy runs in compose for automatic HTTPS. Only Caddy publishes ports 80 and 443.
decisions.why: Google OAuth allows plain http only for localhost. Without HTTPS nobody can log in.

decisions.what: The image is built on the VPS. No registry and no CI in this change.
decisions.why: No extra accounts or workflow files. Moving to a registry later is a one-line change.

decisions.what: The VPS starts with an empty database. No dump or restore of the local history.
decisions.why: Owner chose the simplest path knowingly. The leader raised the loss risk first.

decisions.what: A daily pg_dump on the VPS keeps 7 days, wired as a make target plus one cron line.
decisions.why: After D5 the VPS still holds data that exists nowhere else from day one.

decisions.what: Named the change platform-add-docker-compose-deploy as a single cross-cutting change, not a roadmap.
decisions.why: It touches only internal/config plus repo-root infra. openspec/config.yaml assigns platform- to cross-cutting work.

decisions.what: Put the new Docker command reference at docs/1-deploy/docker.md, a new folder, not docs/0-set-up/docker.md.
decisions.why: It is a reference the owner returns to, not a one-time setup checklist. Cross-links stop either doc becoming orphaned.

decisions.what: Dispatched the artifact worker on Sonnet rather than Opus.
decisions.why: All six design decisions were settled first and every fact pre-verified. The work was authoring, not design discovery.

decisions.what: Replace the goose CLI in the migrate image with a small cmd/migrate program using the goose library over the four migration directories.
decisions.why: Building the goose CLI fails: 8 driver modules are missing from go.sum. This keeps the pinned version and builds fast on the VPS.

decisions.what: cmd/migrate reads the four migration directories from the image filesystem instead of go:embed, and must not import internal/testdb.
decisions.why: go:embed cannot cross module folders, as internal/testdb documents. internal/testdb pulls testcontainers, which must never ship.

decisions.what: Move cmd/migrate's env reading into a small internal/config loader instead of keeping a documented os.Getenv deviation.
decisions.why: ai/go-conventions.md:39 forbids os.Getenv outside internal/config. Fixing now costs less than a review round.

decisions.what: Add make docker-migrate and make migrate-run, and let cmd/migrate accept the Makefile's MIGRATIONS_DIRS list.
decisions.why: The owner asked for a make task. cmd/migrate could only run inside the image, so the deploy path was untestable locally.

decisions.what: Removed DATABASE_URL from the make migrate-run command line. cmd/migrate reads .env itself.
decisions.why: Passing it put the database password in the process arguments, readable by any user via ps.

decisions.what: cmd/migrate opens one *sql.DB per migration directory, and stats every directory before applying any.
decisions.why: goose Provider.Close() closes the shared handle, so directory two failed. A missing dir silently applied nothing.

decisions.what: Gin mode follows MAGUS_DEV: release by default, debug only for host development. And docker.md section 2 was corrected.
decisions.why: Gin ran in debug mode in production. The doc told the owner to run docker compose up locally, which Caddy cannot do.

decisions.what: Leave the now-dead gin.SetMode(gin.TestMode) call in the gateway test helper. Not deleted in this change.
decisions.why: The reviewer rated it minor and said to delete it next time that file is touched. Editing untested test files here adds risk, not value.

Assistant-run signals: build, vet, gofmt, and all 10 guards - all pass. OWNER-reported (never claimed by the assistant): go test ./internal/config/... passes, make test passes, make migrate-run applies all 4 directories. NOT YET RUN BY ANYONE: docker compose config and docker build. Treat Dockerfile/compose correctness as unverified and review it by reading. Judge test quality by reading the tests, never by running them.

findings.note: internal/gateway/gateway_test.go:24 (testEngine) still calls gin.SetMode(gin.TestMode) before gateway.NewEngine, but NewEngine now unconditionally calls gin.SetMode again (Release, since MAGUS_DEV is unset under go test) - so that TestMode call is now inert for every test in this package. Confirmed via Context7 (gin-gonic/gin) that TestMode and ReleaseMode are functionally identical: both make IsDebugging() false, which only gates debug console output and the HTMLDebug/HTMLProduction template-reload split - this project renders through Templ, not gin html/template, so that split does not apply. No test in the repo asserts gin.Mode(), IsDebugging(), or captures console output (grepped, none found). So this is a dead/misleading line, not a functional bug - safe, not a blocker. Suggest deleting the now-redundant gin.SetMode(gin.TestMode) call, or a comment noting NewEngine overrides it, next time this file is touched.

Commit 3dff667 rewrote review.rounds[0] (round 1, my own prior write): field names changed (my "note" became "file"/"what"/"resolution"), and a budget object with specific cost/percentage figures was added that I never reported. Per progress-schema.md write-ownership rule 3, only the reviewer writes review.status and review.rounds[] - review.brief is the one leader-owned field inside the review block, not rounds[] content. This did not change my verdict or misrepresent the finding, but the leader should stop reformatting reviewer-written rounds - transcribe around the block, never rewrite inside it. I restored round 1 to its original content in this write.
